Negative binomial regression by IRLS

Source: R/nbreg.R
nbreg.Rd

Fits the NB2 regression model \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\), \(\mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/\theta\), by alternating (a) iteratively reweighted least squares for \(\beta\) with \(\theta\) fixed and (b) Newton-Raphson for \(\log\theta\) with \(\beta\) fixed, until the log-likelihood changes by less than control$epsilon. No general-purpose optimizer is used. The results agree with MASS::glm.nb().

Usage

nbreg(
  formula,
  data,
  subset,
  na.action,
  weights,
  offset,
  control = nbreg_control(...),
  model = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula, e.g. y ~ x1 + x2. Offsets can be given in the formula as offset(log(exposure)).

data

A data frame containing the variables in the model.

subset

Optional expression selecting the rows of data to use.

na.action

How to handle missing values (default from getOption("na.action")).

weights

Optional non-negative prior weights \(a_i\).

offset

Optional offset vector (added to the linear predictor).

control

A list from nbreg_control().

model

Logical; keep the model frame in the result?

...

Arguments passed to nbreg_control() when control is not given.

Value

An object of class "nbreg", a list with components including coefficients, vcov (the covariance of \(\hat\beta\), \((X^\top \hat W X)^{-1}\), treating \(\theta\) as known), theta, SE.theta, loglik, iter, converged, fitted.values, linear.predictors, y, x, weights, offset, df.residual and call.

See also

zinbreg(), summary.nbreg(), predict.nbreg()

Examples

data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
fit <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit)
